primitives.name: Partial Field Registration
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Partial field registration**: detect visible track lane lines (OpenCV Hough), compute one vanishing point, then construct a dense set of candidate camera calibrations consistent with that vanishing point (1° azimuth increments; elevation/roll/FoV solved to match; translation fitted to lane positions).
primitives.assumptions: Static camera; known field markings; lane lines visible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When lane markings are occluded or absent.

layer2.mapping: Maps 2D image features to 3D camera parameters via geometric constraints, enabling pose lifting under partial observability.
layer2.telemetry: Vanishing point accuracy, lane endpoint reprojection error.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Fundamental ambiguity result (Figure 2): identical image pixels produced by 3D skeletons whose right-leg angle differs by 7.8° — provably unrecoverable without scene geometry.

The paper introduces partial field registration to mitigate this by leveraging visible lane markings to constrain camera calibration. This enables a ray-cast lifting process that projects 2D joints into 3D space while respecting limb length constraints. The method exploits the fact that even with limited field visibility, a single vanishing point can define a family of consistent camera poses. By resolving the remaining degree of freedom through static camera assumptions, the system achieves kinematically valid 3D poses. The fundamental ambiguity bound of 7.8 degrees highlights the theoretical limit when such constraints are absent. This approach bridges the gap between learned 2D-to-3D mappings and physically grounded reconstruction, particularly useful for broadcast footage where full field registration is infeasible.
